title: Merge sorted lists with a fixed order for equal keys
levels: Meets every requirement in the brief
Misses at least one requirement in the brief

cases.rationale: flat() lays the elements out in list order and the stable sort keeps that order among equal keys, which is exactly the required tie order, in a new array.
The <= test lets a later list win ties, so the brief's example mergeSorted([[a1], [b1, c2], [d1]]) returns [d1, b1, a1, c2] instead of [a1, b1, d1, c2].
mergeTwo appends only the rest of right, so mergeSorted on lists with keys [1, 5, 9] and [2, 3] drops 5 and 9 and returns three elements instead of five.
A min-heap ordered by key, list index and position emits every element in key order with the required tie order and only reads the inputs.
